D.treatment: more than one bottom-out hint across 8 problems
D.comparison: no more than one bottom-out hint across 8 problems

cells.quote: Our results indicate that there are two types of students who wheel -spin: first, students who do not request any hints in at least one problem but request more than one bottom-out hint across any 8 problems in the problem set;
cells.note: The study reports a behavioral association rather than a manipulated intervention; no printed effect size for this contrast appears in the supplied study text.

D.treatment: short delays between solving problems of the same skill

cells.quote: second, students who never request two or more bottom out hints across any 8 problems, do not request any hints in at least one problem, but who engage in relatively short delays between solving problems of the same skill.
cells.note: The study reports a behavioral association rather than a manipulated spacing intervention; no printed effect size for this contrast appears in the supplied study text.

O.outcome_detail: passing versus failing the first ARRS retention test after mastery opportunities

cells.quote: Specifically, Beck & Gong (2013) identified wheel-spinning as occurring among students who had 10 or more skill opportunities without mastering a given mathematics concept and found that approximately 38% of students did not master a given skill after 10 practice opportunities and were thus potentially wheel -spinning.
cells.note: The paper operationalizes productive persistence as mastery followed by passing ARRS and wheel-spinning as failure to pass ARRS or failure to achieve mastery; this is an outcome-based classification, not a randomized comparison.
